examples.en: The farmer feeds hay to the cows.
The warehouse is full of piled-up hay.
The horse smelled the hay and came closer.
Hay gets moldy if it gets wet in the rain.
This cushion is stuffed with hay.
The children played on top of a pile of hay.

explain: 소나 말 같은 가축의 사료로 쓰려고 베어서 말려 둔 풀이에요. 벼 같은 곡식을 거둔 뒤에 남는 줄기인 '짚'과는 달라요. 일상에서는 '말린 풀'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is grass that has been cut and dried to feed livestock such as cows and horses. It differs from '짚' (straw), the stalks left after harvesting grain like rice. In daily talk people sometimes just say '말린 풀' (dried grass).

examples.en: A hedgehog has spines on its body.
My friend keeps a hedgehog as a pet.
The hedgehog got scared and curled into a ball.
I almost got pricked by a hedgehog's spines.

examples.ko: 고슴도치와 토끼 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like more, a hedgehog or a rabbit?
I saw a picture of a cute hedgehog.

explain: 고슴도치는 가시 때문에 속담에도 나오는 동물이에요. 비슷하게 가시가 있는 '호저'는 몸이 더 크고 가시도 길어서 다른 동물이에요.

phrases.example: 아무리 말썽쟁이여도 부모에게는 예뻐요. 고슴도치도 제 새끼는 함함하다고 하잖아요.
phrases.en: Even a hedgehog thinks its own young are silky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자식은 누구에게나 예뻐 보인다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning every parent thinks their own child is lovely.
phrases.en_equiv: every crow thinks its own young the fairest

explain_en: The hedgehog appears in a Korean proverb because of its spines. A 호저 (porcupine) also has spines but is bigger with longer quills, so it is a different animal.

examples.en: It's always shady under the tree, so it's cool.
Let's rest a bit in the shade before we go.

examples.ko: 건물 때문에 방이 일 년 내내 그늘져요.
examples.en: The room is shaded all year round because of the building.

examples.ko: 그늘지지 않은 자리를 찾아서 돗자리를 폈어요.
examples.en: I found a spot that wasn't shaded and spread out the mat.
The child's face looked gloomy, so I was worried.
If it's shaded, laundry doesn't dry well.

explain: 햇빛이 가려져 어두워진다는 뜻 외에, 표정이나 마음이 어두워 보일 때도 써요. 햇볕이 잘 드는 곳은 '양지바르다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Besides sunlight being blocked, it's also used when someone's expression or mood looks dark. A place that gets plenty of sunshine is called '양지바르다'.

examples.ko: 이 약은 무지무지하게 써서 먹기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This medicine is so incredibly bitter that it's hard to take.

examples.ko: 무지무지한 눈이 쏟아져서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: Enormous amounts of snow are falling, so cars can't get through.

examples.ko: 그 가게 앞에 무지무지하게 긴 줄이 있어요.
examples.en: There's an incredibly long line in front of that shop.

examples.ko: 이번 달 일이 무지무지해서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: This month's workload is enormous, so I'm overwhelmed.
A huge crowd gathered at the amusement park.
Everyone is worn out from the tremendous heat.

explain: 양이나 정도가 어마어마할 때 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. '무지무지한 + 명사', '무지무지하게 + 서술어'로 쓰고, '엄청나다'와 비슷하지만 말하듯 가벼운 느낌이에요. 부사 '무지무지'는 따로 있어서 '무지무지 덥다'처럼 바로 붙여요.
explain_en: It is a spoken word for when an amount or degree is enormous. It is used as '무지무지한 + noun' or '무지무지하게 + predicate', and is similar to '엄청나다' but with a lighter, chatty feel. The adverb '무지무지' is a separate word, used directly as in '무지무지 덥다'.

examples.en: I saw fireflies for the first time in the countryside on a summer night.
Fireflies glow twinkling in the grass.

examples.ko: 아이들이 손전등 대신 반디 불빛으로 놀았대요.
examples.en: I heard the children played by the light of fireflies instead of a flashlight.

examples.ko: 깨끗한 물가에서만 반디를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see fireflies only near clean water.
I went to a firefly festival and enjoyed the lights.

examples.ko: 요즘은 도시에서 반디가 거의 안 보여요.
examples.en: These days, fireflies are hardly seen in the city.

explain: '반딧불이'가 정확한 곤충 이름이고, '반디'는 그것을 줄인 말이에요. 빛은 '반딧불'이라고 해요. 시골이나 깨끗한 환경을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The exact insect name is 반딧불이, and 반디 is the shortened form. The light it gives off is called 반딧불. It often comes up when talking about the countryside or clean nature.

examples.en: The sunlight reflects off the window and dazzles my eyes.
The mountain looks reflected in the lake.
The sound bounces off the wall and echoes.

examples.ko: 거울에 반사된 빛 때문에 방이 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: The room got brighter from the light reflected by the mirror.

examples.ko: 눈 위에서 반사되는 빛은 아주 강해요.
examples.en: The light reflected off the snow is very strong.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 불빛이 길에 반사될 거예요.
examples.en: When it rains, the lights will reflect on the road.

explain: 빛, 소리, 열이 어떤 면에 부딪혀 튕겨 나올 때 써요. 능동형은 '반사하다'예요. 생각이나 감정을 되돌아본다는 뜻의 영어 reflect와 달리, 한국어 '반사되다'는 주로 빛이나 소리 같은 물리적인 현상에 써요.
explain_en: Use it when light, sound, or heat hits a surface and bounces back; the active form is 반사하다. Unlike English reflect, it is not used for thinking back on ideas or feelings; it is mainly for physical phenomena such as light and sound.

examples.en: When spring came, the seeds began to germinate.
Germinated brown rice is softer than regular brown rice.
I chose seeds with a high germination rate.
This seed takes about a week to sprout.
The seed of the new business was a small conversation.
Bean sprouts are grown by using the germination of beans.

explain: 일상에서는 '싹이 트다', '싹이 나다'라고 말하고, '발아'는 과학이나 농업 이야기에서 많이 써요. 새로운 생각이나 움직임이 처음 생기는 것을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '싹이 트다' or '싹이 나다', while '발아' is common in science and farming. It can also be used figuratively for a new idea or movement first appearing.

examples.en: A big chestnut tree stands on the mountain path.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 밤나무 아래에서 밤을 주워요.
examples.en: When autumn comes, we pick up chestnuts under the chestnut tree.

examples.ko: 할아버지 밭 뒤에 밤나무 몇 그루가 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few chestnut trees behind Grandfather's field.

examples.ko: 밤나무 꽃은 초여름에 피고 냄새가 독특해요.
examples.en: Chestnut blossoms bloom in early summer and have a distinctive smell.

examples.ko: 이 밤나무는 백 년도 더 됐대요.
examples.en: I heard this chestnut tree is over a hundred years old.
A chestnut burr fell from the chestnut tree.

explain: '밤(night)'과 '밤(chestnut)'은 소리가 같아요. '밤나무'는 열매 밤이 열리는 나무라서 헷갈릴 일이 없지만, '밤이 맛있다' 같은 문장은 앞뒤 말을 보고 뜻을 구분해요.
explain_en: '밤' meaning night and '밤' meaning chestnut sound the same. '밤나무' is the tree that bears chestnuts, so it is not confusing, but in a sentence like '밤이 맛있다' you tell the meaning from the context.

examples.en: A nest hangs from the tree.
I found a bee nest under the eaves of the house.
This snack is shaped like a honeycomb.
You get honey from the hive.
Don't go near the nest.

examples.ko: 벌집은 작은 육각형 방으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: A honeycomb is made of small hexagonal cells.

explain: 벌이 사는 집은 '벌집'이고, 사람이 꿀을 얻으려고 만든 상자는 '벌통'이에요. 구멍이 많이 뚫린 모양을 '벌집'에 빗대어 '벌집이 되다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 뉴스가 나오자 온 동네가 벌집을 쑤셔 놓은 것 같았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 큰 소동이 나서 시끄럽고 정신없는 모습을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a place suddenly thrown into noisy confusion.

explain_en: The home of bees or wasps is a 벌집, while the box people make to collect honey is a 벌통. A thing full of holes is also compared to it, as in '벌집이 되다'.

examples.en: The autumn mountains turned a deep red.

examples.ko: 저녁 하늘이 붉디붉어서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: The evening sky was so deeply red that I took lots of photos.
I was given a single deep red rose.
I'm embarrassed, so my face is bright red.
The deep red maple leaves have all fallen before I knew it.
The inside of a pomegranate is deep red and tastes sour.

explain: 노을, 단풍, 장미, 피처럼 색이 강하고 선명할 때 느낌을 살려 써요. 말할 때는 '새빨갛다', '빨갛다'가 더 흔해요. '높디높다', '길디길다'처럼 같은 형용사를 반복해서 강조하는 꼴이에요.
explain_en: It brings out a strong, vivid color, as in a sunset, autumn leaves, a rose or blood. In speech, '새빨갛다' and '빨갛다' are more common. It has the same pattern as '높디높다' and '길디길다', repeating the adjective for emphasis.

examples.ko: 코끼리 상아를 노리는 밀렵이 아직도 문제예요.
examples.en: Poaching for elephant tusks is still a problem.

examples.ko: 이 피아노 건반은 예전에 상아로 만들었대요.
examples.en: I heard piano keys used to be made of ivory.

examples.ko: 상아 색깔의 원피스가 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: The ivory-colored dress suits you really well.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 상아로 조각한 작은 장식품을 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum, I saw a small ornament carved from ivory.

examples.ko: 상아 거래는 많은 나라에서 금지되어 있어요.
examples.en: Ivory trade is banned in many countries.

examples.ko: 새끼 코끼리는 아직 상아가 많이 자라지 않았어요.
examples.en: The baby elephant's tusks haven't grown much yet.

explain: 코끼리 같은 동물의 길게 자란 이빨과 그것으로 만든 재료를 모두 가리켜요. 색 이름으로 '상아색'이라고도 하고, 외래어 '아이보리'도 같이 써요.
explain_en: It refers both to the long tusks of animals such as elephants and to the material made from them. It is also used as a color name, '상아색', and the loanword '아이보리' is used as well.

examples.ko: 봄이 되자 산과 들이 생동하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When spring came, the mountains and fields began to come alive.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 인물들이 금방 움직일 것처럼 생동해요.
examples.en: The figures in this painting look so alive they seem about to move.
The street that had been full of life turned quiet at night.

examples.ko: 색을 힘 있게 쓴 덕분에 그림 속 바다가 생동했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the bold use of color, the sea in the painting came alive.

examples.ko: 생동하는 느낌을 살리려고 사진을 다시 찍었어요.
examples.en: I retook the photo to bring out a lively feel.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 장면이 생동해서 눈을 뗄 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The scenes in this movie are so vivid that I couldn't look away.

explain: 동사로 쓰기보다 '생동감이 있다/넘치다', '생동하는 ~' 모양으로 많이 써요. 그림, 풍경, 글을 묘사할 때 어울리고, 대화에서는 '생생하다', '활기차다'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: It is used less as a plain verb and more in forms like '생동감이 있다/넘치다' and '생동하는 ~'. It suits descriptions of paintings, scenery and writing, while in conversation '생생하다' or '활기차다' feels easier.

examples.en: The child's rice bowl is always heaped full.
Dust lay thick on the desk.
It was hard shoveling the deeply piled snow.
I was given a plate heaped with food.

examples.ko: 음식이 너무 수북해서 뚜껑이 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: The food is piled so high that the lid won't close.
It's not heaped up, but there's plenty of rice.

explain: '가득하다'는 꽉 찬 것이고, '수북하다'는 위로 솟을 만큼 쌓인 모양이에요. '소복하다'는 눈처럼 더 얕고 포근하게 쌓인 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '가득하다' means full, while '수북하다' means piled up higher than the container. '소복하다' feels shallower and softer, as with a light layer of snow.

examples.en: The leaves on the plant are wilting.
The lettuce is so limp that I hesitate to eat it.

examples.ko: 시들시들한 꽃에 물을 주니 다시 살아났어요.
examples.en: When I watered the drooping flower, it revived.
The plants are wilting because of the heat.
Why do you look so droopy today?

examples.ko: 시들시들하던 나무가 비가 오자 힘을 되찾았어요.
examples.en: The wilting tree regained its strength once it rained.

explain: 식물이 말라서 축 처진 상태를 말하지만, 사람이 기운이 없어 보일 때도 비유로 써요. 활용은 '시들시들해요, 시들시들한'이에요. 부사 '시들시들'도 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It describes a plant that has dried out and drooped, and it is also used figuratively when a person looks drained. The forms are 시들시들해요 and 시들시들한. Also learn the adverb 시들시들.

examples.en: Now that it's winter, the branches are very bare.

examples.ko: 감나무의 앙상한 가지 사이로 초가지붕이 보여요.
examples.en: A thatched roof can be seen between the bare branches of the persimmon tree.
I've lost weight lately and my arms have become bony.
A skinny, bony cat was in the alley.

examples.ko: 할머니의 앙상한 손을 잡으니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Holding my grandmother's bony hand made my heart ache.

examples.ko: 잎이 다 떨어져서 가지만 앙상하게 남았어요.
examples.en: All the leaves fell, and only the bare branches remain.

explain: 잎이 다 떨어진 가지나 살이 빠져 뼈가 드러난 몸처럼, 있어야 할 것이 없어 초라하고 안쓰러운 느낌이에요. 사람에게 쓰면 '말랐다'보다 더 안타까운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes things that lack what they should have, such as branches with no leaves or a body so thin that the bones show, with a pitiful feel. For people it sounds more sorrowful than simply '말랐다' (thin).

examples.en: A loud sound of thunder rang out in the sky.

examples.ko: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 우레와 같은 박수를 보냈어요.
examples.en: When the show ended, the audience gave thunderous applause.

examples.ko: 우레 같은 함성이 경기장을 가득 채웠어요.
examples.en: A thunderous roar filled the stadium.

examples.ko: 멀리서 우레가 울리더니 곧 비가 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: Thunder rumbled in the distance, and soon the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 골이 들어가자 우레 같은 환호가 터졌어요.
examples.en: When the goal went in, a thunderous cheer erupted.

examples.ko: 그의 목소리는 우레처럼 커서 모두가 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: His voice was as loud as thunder, and everyone was startled.

explain: '천둥'과 같은 뜻의 말이지만 지금은 '우레와 같은 박수'처럼 크고 힘찬 소리를 비유할 때 주로 써요. 하늘에서 치는 소리를 평소에 말할 때는 보통 '천둥'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 연설이 끝나자 우레와 같은 박수가 터졌어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박수 소리가 천둥처럼 크고 힘차게 울릴 때 쓰는 표현이에요. 공연이나 연설이 끝난 뒤 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for applause so loud and powerful that it sounds like thunder. It often appears in news and writing after a performance or speech.

explain_en: It means the same as '천둥' (thunder), but nowadays it is mainly used in comparisons for loud, powerful sounds, as in '우레와 같은 박수'. In everyday talk about the sound in the sky, people usually say '천둥'.

examples.en: Many twigs broke in the wind last night.

examples.ko: 나무의 잔가지를 쳐 주면 더 잘 자라요.
examples.en: If you trim a tree's twigs, it grows better.
At the campsite I made kindling out of dry twigs.
A sparrow perched on a twig is chirping.

examples.ko: 큰 줄기만 남기고 잔가지는 다 잘라 냈어요.
examples.en: I cut off all the twigs and left only the main trunk.
Please clear away the twigs that fell on the road too.

explain: 굵은 줄기나 큰 가지에서 갈라져 나온 가늘고 작은 가지를 말해요. 이야기를 할 때 핵심이 아닌 부분은 '곁가지'라고 비유해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the thin, small branches that split off from a thick trunk or big branch. When talking about a story, the non-essential parts are sometimes called '곁가지' as a metaphor.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 바다 조망이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This hotel has a really good sea view.
I chose this apartment because I was drawn to the view.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 도시 전체의 조망을 즐겼어요.
examples.en: I enjoyed the view of the whole city from the summit.
The view isn't great because the building in front blocks it.
A dispute arose among neighbors over the right to a view.

examples.ko: 전망대에서 본 조망 덕분에 피곤이 싹 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The view from the observatory made my tiredness disappear.

explain: 높은 곳에서 멀리까지 내다보이는 경치를 말해요. '전망'과 비슷하지만 '전망'은 앞날의 예측이라는 뜻도 있어서, 풍경만 가리킬 때 '조망'이 더 분명해요. 부동산이나 숙소 소개에서 '조망이 좋다', '조망권'으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means the scenery you can see far away from a high place. It is similar to '전망', but '전망' can also mean a forecast of the future, so '조망' is clearer when you mean only the scenery. It is common in real estate and lodging descriptions as '조망이 좋다' or '조망권'.

examples.en: I saw a sea horse for the first time at the aquarium.
The sea horse is holding onto seaweed with its tail.

examples.ko: 아이가 해마 모양 인형을 갖고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: The child wanted a sea horse-shaped doll.
My friend said the sea horse looks like a horse.
I want to swim with sea horses in the ocean.

examples.ko: 해마의 수컷이 새끼를 낳는다는 사실을 알았어요.
examples.en: I learned that the male sea horse gives birth to the young.

explain: 뇌에서 기억을 맡는 부분도 '해마'라고 불러서 같은 소리의 말이에요. 문장 속 내용을 보면 동물인지 뇌인지 알 수 있어요. 동물 해마는 머리 모양이 말을 닮아서 이름에 '마'(말)가 들어가요.
explain_en: The part of the brain that handles memory is also called 해마, so the same word has two meanings. The context tells you whether it is the animal or the brain. The animal has 마, meaning horse, in its name because its head looks like a horse.

en: in a rush of heat; hotly; burningly

examples.ko: 방에 들어가자 후끈 더운 공기가 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: When I entered the room, I felt a wave of hot air.
I was embarrassed and my face flushed hot.
I turned on the heater and the room warmed up quickly.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 먹었더니 온몸이 후끈 더워졌어요.
examples.en: After eating spicy food, my whole body got hot.

examples.ko: 열차 문이 열리자 후끈 열기가 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: When the train door opened, a rush of heat came in.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears burned.

explain: '후끈 달아오르다', '후끈 더워지다'처럼 갑자기 열기가 확 느껴질 때 써요. 부끄러움이나 화로 얼굴이 뜨거워질 때도 쓰고, 분위기가 뜨거울 때 '분위기가 후끈 달아오르다'라고도 해요. 약하게 따뜻한 건 '따끈'이 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when heat suddenly hits you, as in '후끈 달아오르다' and '후끈 더워지다'. It also fits a face heating up from embarrassment or anger, and a heated mood, '분위기가 후끈 달아오르다'. For gentle warmth, '따끈' fits better.
